q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most. 37.1% of their videos outperformed their baseline (n=62 videos), against 18.4% for mid-size channels (n=38) and 0% for large ones (n=17). Average relative lift follows the same order: 6.42 for small, 1.11 for mid, and 0.54 for large.

Audiences are moderately happy everywhere, and mid-size channels are happiest:
- Small: net sentiment +14.5 (43.9% positive, 29.3% negative, n=846 product-side comments)
- Mid: +22 (47.8% positive, 25.5% negative, n=490)
- Large: +10 (39.2% positive, 28.8% negative, n=222)

Caveat: the large-channel group is small (17 videos), so treat its 0% rate cautiously. Small channels' high average lift may also be pulled up by a few big hits. These are associations, not causes.
sql: WITH vids AS (SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size, p.outperformer, p.rel_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'), lift AS (SELECT size, COUNT(*) AS n_videos_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift FROM vids WHERE outperformer IS NOT NULL GROUP BY size), sent AS (SELECT v.size, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN vids v ON v.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY v.size) SELECT l.size, l.n_videos_with_baseline, l.outperformer_rate, l.avg_rel_lift, s.n_product_side, s.pct_positive, s.pct_negative, CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN s.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment FROM lift l LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size=l.size ORDER BY l.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions is the most reliable format for mid-sized channels. It has the largest sample (n=15) and a 33% outperformer rate (5 of 15), with an average relative lift of 1.42.

Explainer/tips has the highest average relative lift (1.91) and the same 33% rate, but that rests on only 3 videos (1 outperformer), so treat it as tentative.

Comparison is next at a 20% rate (1 of 5) and a 1.33 lift, also a small sample.

Keynote recap (n=4), upgrade advice (n=6), meme shorts (n=2), durability test (n=1) and "other" (n=2) had no outperformers. Their average lifts ran from 0.08 to 0.80, though most of those samples are tiny.

Caveat: these are associations from a small set of videos, not proof that format causes the results.
sql: SELECT c.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(p.outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(p.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(p.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, ROUND(AVG(p.lift),3) AS avg_lift, SUM(CASE WHEN p.outperformer=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_outperformers FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' AND p.rel_lift IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
The two most negative high-lift videos are:

1. WSJ News, "I Tried Apple's First Folding iPhone. Here Are 3 Takeaways." (first impressions). Lift is 14.06 (relative lift 2.4). Net sentiment is -35, with 18% positive and 53% negative (n=17).

2. Both Sides of the Tech, "Apple Might Not Make Another iPhone Duo..." (upgrade advice). Lift is 29.77 (relative lift 5.1). Net sentiment is -27, with 27% positive and 55% negative (n=11).

Shawn Shaman's comparison video and Both Sides of the Tech's durability video are close behind, both at -25.

Caveat: each video has only 11 to 17 product-side comments, so these scores are rough. Lift and sentiment are also only associated, not causally linked.
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT c.video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, AVG(c.sentiment='positive') AS pos, AVG(c.sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments c WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND c.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY c.video_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=10) SELECT ct.video_id, ct.title, cr.name AS creator_name, ct.format, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pos,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.neg,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(s.pos-s.neg,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content ct JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=ct.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=ct.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=ct.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, p.rel_lift DESC LIMIT 10

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
Largest topics: "Excitement and durability tests" leads (n=297, 18.9% of topic comments), then "Praise for the review" (n=267, 17.0%) and "Price and value" (n=184, 11.7%).

Fastest growing this week: Excitement and durability tests is first in absolute gain, rising from 29 to 160 comments (+131, up about 452%). Price and value is second (22 to 106, up about 382%), and the Samsung Fold comparison is third (17 to 88, up about 418%). By percentage alone, Apple copying Android accusations (7 to 47, up about 571%) and Folding animation praise (6 to 38, up about 533%) rise fastest, but from small bases.

Inner screen and crease and Duo comparisons and video content are growing slowest.

Caveat: this is a comment sample, and small starting counts make the percentages jumpy.
sql: WITH sc AS (SELECT c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT max(d) AS m FROM sc), agg AS (SELECT sc.topic_id, count(*) AS n_total, sum(CASE WHEN d>m-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, sum(CASE WHEN d<=m-7 AND d>m-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prev_week FROM sc, mx WHERE sc.topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY sc.topic_id) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, ROUND(1.0*a.n_total/SUM(a.n_total) OVER (),3) AS share_of_topic_comments, a.n_this_week, a.n_prev_week, a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week AS change_abs, CASE WHEN a.n_prev_week>0 THEN ROUND(1.0*(a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week)/a.n_prev_week,3) END AS growth_pct, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY a.n_total DESC) AS size_rank, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week DESC) AS growth_rank FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id ORDER BY a.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
a:
Duo sits clearly above general event and "other" content but below the competitor foldable. Its net sentiment is +21 (46% positive, 26% negative, n=1,411 comments across 129 videos).

- Competitor foldable: +33 (50% positive, 18% negative), but only n=40 comments across 3 videos, so treat it as directional.
- iPhone 18 Pro: +17 (42% positive, 25% negative), but n=12 across 2 videos, too small to read much into.
- General event content: -9 (29% positive, 38% negative), n=86.
- Other: -12 (26% positive, 38% negative), n=65.

Duo is the only topic with a large sample, so its score is the most reliable. These figures come from a sample of comments and show associations, not causes.
sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(DISTINCT c.video_id) AS n_videos, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN 'ok' ELSE 'n<10' END AS n_check FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY (c.topic='duo') DESC, n_product_side DESC LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
Fans like the anticipation most, along with the folding animation. The "Excitement and durability tests" topic has a net sentiment of +34 (n=247; 52% positive, 17% negative). Folding animation praise is +30 (n=92; 54% positive, 24% negative).

Price and value draws the most criticism among the larger topics. Its net is +12 (n=157; 46% positive, 34% negative). The Samsung Fold comparison has the highest negative share, 37%, but a smaller n of 57 and a net of +14. Apple-copying accusations have the weakest net, +8 (n=52), also a small sample.

Caveat: every topic nets positive, and the same topics appear on both the liked and criticised lists. So these are relative differences, and the sentiment may be about the topic debate rather than the phone itself.
sql: WITH c AS (SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.summary, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(cm.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(cm.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg FROM comments cm JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=cm.video_id JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=cm.topic_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value') AND t.pool='product' GROUP BY t.topic_id, t.name, t.summary), r AS (SELECT *, ROUND(n_pos*1.0/n,3) AS pct_pos, ROUND(n_neg*1.0/n,3) AS pct_neg, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY n_pos DESC) AS rp, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY n_neg DESC) AS rn FROM c) SELECT 'liked' AS side, name, summary, n, n_pos, n_neg, pct_pos, pct_neg FROM r WHERE rp<=8 UNION ALL SELECT 'criticised' AS side, name, summary, n, n_pos, n_neg, pct_pos, pct_neg FROM r WHERE rn<=8 LIMIT 40
